title: DROP VIEW
description: DROP VIEW removes a saved view definition - it never touches the underlying tables' data, since a view was never storing a copy of it. The fixtures already include a view named `department_headcounts` - drop it.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: DROP VIEW
Same idea as DROP TABLE, just the VIEW keyword instead - DROP VIEW <name> takes just the view's name, no WHERE clause.
Use DROP VIEW followed by the exact view name, department_headcounts.
expected_behavior: department_headcounts no longer exists as a view; employees itself is completely untouched.
explanation: Because a view is just a saved query, dropping it is instant and never risks losing data - the real table it queried is exactly as it was.

hidden_tests.check_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM information_schema.views WHERE table_schema = 'fixtures' AND table_name = 'department_headcounts'
hidden_tests.label: department_headcounts view is gone
